title: Layer-aware microbatching and ring collective scheduling proposal
content:
Summary:

This is a working proposal for a practical multi-GPU serving strategy that combines layer-aware microbatching with an adaptive ring-collective scheduler. Goal: reduce tail latency variability and per-token cost for large autoregressive models under mixed request sizes and heterogeneous hardware interconnects. This doc focuses on three levers: microbatch placement, KV cache partitioning aligned with pipeline/tensor stages, and dynamic NCCL collective selection based on per-layer communication patterns.

Why this problem:
- In production inference we see latency jitter when requests of varying sequence lengths and batch sizes compete for the same GPUs.
- Naive sharding (round-robin or static layer splits) leads to imbalanced NVLink/NCCL utilization: some ranks become bandwidth-starved while others idle.
- KV cache traffic during long-context calls interferes with streaming small requests; eviction/reconstruction cost is high when KV shards are not colocated with the compute that needs them.

Design principles:
1) Stage affinity: co-locate KV shards with the pipeline stage(s) that use them most often to reduce cross-rank fetches.
2) Microbatching locality: microbatches should be scheduled so that contiguous microbatches that traverse the same layer group use the same NCCL topology, minimizing re-config costs.
3) Adaptive collective selection: choose between ring all-reduce, tree-based collectives, or pairwise send/recv per-layer based on message size and topology (NVLink vs PCIe).
4) Graceful fallbacks: when interconnect capacity is constrained, prefer compute replication on cheap models or fallback to lower-precision kernel paths rather than blocking on large allreduce.

High-level architecture:
- Scheduler component (run-time module): maintains a lightweight profile of recent layer-wise communication sizes and per-rank latency. Exposes an API: suggest_topology(layer_id, message_size) -> topology_hint.
- KV placement manager: maps KV shards to ranks with an LRU-aware hotness metric. Provides APIs to pin/unpin shards and to prefetch on canary requests.
- Microbatch orchestrator: splits incoming request batches into microbatches, assigns microbatch routes (which set of ranks/stages), and batches compatible microbatches together for a given NCCL topology.

Key mechanisms (detailed):
1) Layer-aware microbatch grouping
- During model load we compute a per-layer expected activation/attention kernel footprint (tokens * hidden_size). We annotate layers with one of three communication classes: tiny (<64KB), medium (64KB-8MB), large (>8MB).
- Incoming requests are tagged at enqueue time with expected per-layer communication profile (fast estimate using seq_len * attention_heads * head_dim).
- The orchestrator groups microbatches that have compatible profiles for the next N layers (configurable, default N=4). Grouping constraint: message size class must match and assigned ranks must share a stable topology hint.
- Benefit: NCCL communicator reuse and fewer topology reconfig ops; better kernel pipelining for tensor-parallel stages.

2) Ring vs tree vs p2p collective selection
- Heuristics:
  * tiny messages: prefer pairwise send/recv to avoid NCCL overhead.
  * medium messages on NVLink-connected ranks: ring all-reduce with chunking tuned to NVLink bandwidth.
  * large messages across PCIe: consider hierarchical allreduce (intra-node ring + inter-node tree) or fallback to sharded-parameter fetch with asynchronous prefetch.
- The scheduler will continuously measure latency for each collective mode per-layer and adjust thresholds (simple exponential moving average over 256 samples).
- NCCL tuning knobs surfaced: chunk_size_bytes, min_ring_step, algorithm_hint (ring/tree), comm_reuse_ttl (seconds). We will expose these to dedicated pools for experimentation.

3) KV cache partitioning and hot-path pinning
- Default: KV cache shards partitioned by contiguous block of layers (layer-range ownership). This minimizes cross-stage lookups for autoregressive decoding.
- Hot-path optimization: for small high-frequency keys (short repeating prompts), replicate the most-recently used KV slices to upto 2 additional ranks (configurable) rather than always fetching from remote. Replication limited by memory budget and TTL policy.
- Eviction: background compaction job merges remote deltas periodically to keep memory footprint stable.

Implementation notes and API sketches:
- config example (pseudo-yaml):
  microbatch:
    max_microbatch_tokens: 2048
    grouping_window_layers: 4
    topology_reuse_ttl_s: 1.5
  nccl_tunables:
    chunk_size_bytes: auto
    algorithm_hint: auto
    perf_probe_interval_s: 10
  kv:
    replication_budget_percent: 6
    hotness_threshold_qps: 50
    prefetch_lookahead_ms: 20

- Runtime API (Python-like):
  topology_hint = scheduler.suggest_topology(layer_id, estimated_message_size)
  route = orchestrator.allocate_microbatch(request, topology_hint)
  kv_manager.pin_shard(shard_id, ranks=[r1,r2])

Experiment plan (short):
1) Small cluster perf probe (4x A100 NVLink node): run mixed client workload (50% small streaming, 30% medium, 20% long-context). Baseline: current static sharding. Measure p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost.
2) Enable layer-aware grouping only, collect metrics.
3) Add adaptive collective selection. Compare benefits and regression modes.
4) Enable KV hot-path replication. Track memory overhead and eviction CPU cost.

Preliminary targets and expectations:
- Aim for 15-25% reduction in p99 latency for mixed workloads on NVLink clusters.
- Expect cost per token delta: +2-6% memory overhead in exchange for 10-18% CPU/pipeline efficiency gains.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How often can we safely reassign KV shard ownership without causing recompute or cache thrash? (Tunable parameter; need experiments).
- Where to draw line between replication and prefetching? For different model sizes the sweet spot will move.
- Implementation complexity: exposing too many NCCL knobs may make runtime brittle. Consider a two-tier approach: safe defaults + experimental knobs under dedicated pool flag.

Rollout strategy:
- Start behind a feature flag in dedicated pools with canary routing.
- Gradual rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 50% traffic while monitoring p99, error rate, GC/memory spikes.
- If p99 regresses >10% or error rate increases >0.1% revert.

Short TODOs (owner tags):

- [Daniel] KV hot-path replication policy sketch + mem estimator (1 week)
- [Mariana] experiment harness for mixed traffic on 4-node NVLink (2 weeks)
- [Ethan] surface NCCL tunables behind 'experimental' flag and add telemetry hooks (1 week)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally exploratory: focus feedback on safety modes, operational signals we should expose (e.g., topology-switch count, per-layer collective latency histograms), and feasibility of adopting replication in Private deployments with tight memory limits.
- Linking to related docs: see multi-gpu sharding playbooks and prior NCCL tuning notes in the serving-runtime folder.

Quick sketches / thought experiments:
- Example worst-case: 64k token long decode interleaved with a burst of 128 single-token streaming requests. Our approach attempts to route the streaming requests to ranks with low current KV-fetch pressure and prioritize pairwise tiny-message handling to keep their tail latency low while long decode proceeds with hierarchical collectives.

Appendix (observability signals to add):
- per-layer message size histogram
- topology_switch_count per minute
- kv_remote_fetch_latency p50/p95/p99 per shard
- replica_memory_utilization and replica_hit_rate
- nccl_mode_selected per-call

End.
